intro:

title: Worker image: apt packages and source offer
intro:
The worker images (Debian trixie, snapshot 20261020T000000Z) include git, sqlite3, jq, curl,
ca-certificates, procps, python3, perl, chromium and chromium-headless-shell. Each package keeps its own licence in
`/usr/share/doc/<package>/copyright` (chromium and chromium-headless-shell, built from one Debian source package, bundle many parts under BSD, LGPL, MPL and GPL
terms). Corresponding source for every Debian package in the image is available as source packages
(`deb-src`) from https://snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian/20261020T000000Z/ and
https://snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian-security/20261020T000000Z/ . This is the written source
offer for the GPL and LGPL parts.

title: Worker image: Python layer (indirect dependencies)
intro: Dev tools installed with pip into the worker image (`docker/stacks/python/Dockerfile`). They run as separate programs and are not part of Capsule's code. Every package, direct or indirect, is in the table above with its resolved version and licence, read from `docs/licenses/python-layer.pip-licenses.json` and `web-layer.pip-licenses.json` (pip-licenses 5.5.5 run on a venv built from the Dockerfile pins, Python 3.13, 2026-11-15). `maintenance/notice_gen.py --scan` fails when a Dockerfile pin and that evidence disagree.

title: Worker image: web layer (indirect dependencies)
intro: Installed into the worker image by `docker/stacks/web/`. Playwright, pyee and greenlet are in the table above, read from `web-layer.pip-licenses.json` and `package-lock.json`.
rows: MIT (npm: Artistic-2.0; bundled dependencies mostly MIT, ISC or BSD)
outro:
The worker images are built on the user's machine, and `.github/workflows/image.yml`
also pushes them to GHCR, so they are distributed. Public GHCR images need a
corresponding-source pointer (for example snapshot.debian.org for the pinned
trixie date) or must stay private. They sit on a Debian trixie slim base plus apt packages (git, sqlite3,
jq, curl, ca-certificates, procps, python3, perl, chromium, chromium-headless-shell). Those are separate
programs under their own licences (some GPL or LGPL), shipped as an aggregate
with Capsule's code and not linked into it; each package's licence file is in the
image under `/usr/share/doc/<package>/copyright`.

title: Services you download separately
intro:
`observability/docker-compose.yml` and the other compose files only name these
container images. Your machine downloads them from their upstream registries when
you start the stack. Their own licences apply, and Capsule does not redistribute
them: no copy of their code or images is in this repository or in a Capsule
release.
rows: BSD-3-Clause (the `infisical-redis` service; replaced Redis 7.4, RSALv2 or SSPLv1, on 2026-11-15)
MIT, except `ee/` directories under the Infisical Enterprise licence

title: CI-only tools (not shipped)
intro:
These run in GitHub Actions or are named in CI configuration. Nothing of them is
in a Capsule artefact.
rows: renovate (hosted app and its config file only)
trivy (CLI, run by trivy-action in image.yml and verify.yml)
Semgrep Rules License v1.0 (not open source; used in CI only, not redistributed, no rule text is in this repository)

title: Host tools you install yourself
intro:
`Brewfile` and `install.sh` name tools such as uv, gh, git, jq, sqlite, node and
ollama. You install them from their own sources under their own licences; Capsule
does not redistribute them.
rows: GPL-2.0-only, installed by the user, not redistributed
GPL-3.0-or-later, installed by the user, not redistributed
OrbStack (default Docker engine), Docker Desktop (optional), Claude Code (orbstack, docker-desktop and claude-code casks)
proprietary, under the user's own terms (OrbStack: free for personal use, paid licence for commercial use), not redistributed
